technical: A Power BI and Fabric planning, analytics and app-building platform with proprietary write-back and multidimensional modeling, acquired by Vena (closed March 26, 2026) and still branded Acterys.
sales: Vena's planning option for teams that work in Power BI rather than Excel. It overlaps directly with Microsoft's Fabric Planning, so be ready to position the two.

technical: Databricks' governed platform for building and running enterprise agents, which now includes the former Mosaic AI Agent Framework, with components such as Supervisor Agent (GA February 10, 2026), Knowledge Assistant and Document Intelligence.
sales: Databricks' toolkit for building AI agents and multi-agent teams. It suits custom agents, which is the point, since a buyer would be building the finance agents themselves.

technical: Google's open-source framework for building single and multi-agent systems as graphs of sub-agents, with MCP and A2A support and deployment to Agent Runtime.
sales: Google's developer toolkit for coding AI agents. It is a building block for teams who plan to write their own finance agents.

technical: Agent Runtime, formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine, hosts agents on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Memory Bank stores long-term user preferences and facts across sessions with revision tracking and IAM-based access control. Sessions and Memory Bank billing began September 1, 2026.
sales: Google's hosting and memory service for custom agents. Its memory is scoped to individual users rather than shared knowledge of how finance plans.

technical: The AgentCore memory service that keeps short-term session events for up to 365 days and extracts long-term semantic, summary, preference and episodic memories, with namespaces that scope memories by organization, team or user. Episodic memory went GA December 2, 2025.
sales: Amazon's well-engineered memory store for AI agents. It knows nothing about finance, so someone has to decide what an assumption or planning decision memory looks like.

technical: Snowflake's separate billing currency for AI services such as Cortex Agents, CoWork and AI Functions, priced at $2.00 with global cross-region routing or $2.20 with regional routing, separate from platform credits, with costs adding up across every service an agent calls.
sales: The meter Snowflake uses to bill AI usage, on top of normal compute. Because an agent's costs stack across several services, the monthly bill is harder to predict than a subscription.

technical: AI.FORECAST is a BigQuery SQL function that produces time-series forecasts using Google's pretrained TimesFM model, GA since September 30, 2025, and TimesFM in Connected Sheets went GA July 1, 2026. AI.KEY_DRIVERS for contribution analysis went GA September 29, 2026.
sales: Google's built-in forecasting that works without training a model. It produces a useful statistical baseline, but turning a baseline into an approved plan still needs a planning process.

technical: A no-code environment in Palantir AIP for creating, testing and deploying AI-powered functions that read and act on Ontology data and can be triggered from applications or automations.
sales: Palantir's point-and-click builder for AI steps. Planning calculations like allocations or spreading would still need to be engineered in it or in code.

technical: Rules that distribute amounts, such as shared costs or targets, from a source across entities, departments or products using bases like headcount, revenue or square footage.
sales: Spreading shared costs like IT or rent across departments fairly. Ask every vendor to show this live, since it is complex to build and not consistently documented in public material.

technical: AWS's managed services for running agents at scale, GA October 13, 2025, including Runtime, Memory, Gateway (which connects to MCP servers), Identity, Observability, Policy guardrails and Evaluations, billed on consumption.
sales: Amazon's industrial-strength plumbing for building AI agents. It is a platform for builders, so every finance-specific piece would be custom.

technical: AWS's agentic business suite, launched as Amazon Quick Suite in October 2025 and later shortened to Amazon Quick, bundling chat, research, automation flows and BI, with semantic datasets added July 7, 2026. It documents no write-back or planning, and it replaces Amazon Q Business, which is closed to new customers.
sales: Amazon's AI assistant and reporting suite, with enterprise plans at $20 or $40 per user plus $250 per account per month. The realistic overlap with Vena is reporting and Q&A, not planning.

technical: AWS's managed cloud data warehouse for SQL analytics, accessible through SageMaker Unified Studio and SageMaker Catalog. Its AI features were not separately researched for this comparison.
sales: Amazon's data warehouse, often where AWS customers keep actuals. Like other warehouses, it stores data for reporting but does not include planning workflow, versions or input.

technical: An immutable log recording who changed which value or object, when, from what to what, and ideally why through comments, covering user, system and AI-initiated changes.
sales: The record auditors and controllers use to answer who changed this number and why. Platform logs track queries and agent actions, but plan-level change history with comments usually has to be built.

technical: Google Cloud's serverless data warehouse, now with conversational analytics (GA June 23, 2026), built-in AI functions such as AI.FORECAST and AI.KEY_DRIVERS, a managed MCP server (GA April 20, 2026) and Iceberg table support.
sales: Google's main data warehouse. It is strong for analysis and forecasting, but its data agents are read-only and there is no native planning application.

technical: Permissions that control read or write access at the level of individual intersections of dimensions, such as letting a manager edit only their own cost center's opex in the current forecast. Vena publicly documents entity-level security, so confirm cell-level detail internally.
sales: Controlling exactly which numbers each person can see and edit in the plan. Data platform row and column policies mainly govern reading, so write permissions by intersection are custom work.

technical: A Google Sheets feature for analyzing BigQuery data through pivots, charts, extracts and scheduled refresh without moving the data into the sheet. Its documentation describes analysis and refresh but not write-back.
sales: Google Sheets connected live to BigQuery for analysis. It does not save planning inputs back to the warehouse, unlike Excel-native planning in Vena.

technical: Google's API for building data agents over BigQuery and Looker, offering text-to-SQL, Looker query generation, a Python code interpreter, context retrieval and charts through stateful and stateless chat. GA June 23, 2026 per its release notes, though one Google blog says August 2026.
sales: Google's developer service for embedding ask-your-data assistants into apps. Like Google's other data agents, it reads data and does not update plans.

technical: Microsoft's low-code platform for building custom agents that publish to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Fabric data agents now plug in as a tool through the Fabric IQ Data MCP, an integration Microsoft announced as GA around September 2026.
sales: Microsoft's builder for custom AI assistants. It is where a Microsoft shop might assemble its own planning agent, which would still need a planning backend to write to.

technical: Snowflake's fully managed agent platform (GA) that runs a plan, tool-use and reflect loop over tools such as Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, stored procedures, sandboxed code and MCP connectors, with persisted threads and feedback capture.
sales: Snowflake's toolkit for building AI agents on Snowflake data. Agents can only change data through procedures a developer writes, so plan updates are a custom build.

technical: Snowflake's text-to-SQL service that answers natural-language questions over semantic views or legacy YAML semantic models, billed per 1,000 messages through its API or by tokens when called from Cortex Agents.
sales: Snowflake's ask-a-question feature for data in Snowflake. Its 90%+ accuracy claim comes from Snowflake's own 2024 test on simple pre-joined data, and it reads data rather than updating plans.

technical: Snowflake's managed search service over text and unstructured data, used as a retrieval tool by Cortex Agents and billed on serving compute per GB per month plus embedding tokens.
sales: Snowflake's search engine that lets AI agents find relevant documents and text. It supports the document side of an AI assistant rather than planning calculations.

technical: A Snowflake runtime context layer that assembles context from query history, object metadata, BI definitions and semantic views, with self-correcting evaluation loops. Snowflake's June 30, 2026 blog says private preview from mid-July 2026, while other sources say GA soon or GA, so status is disputed.
sales: Snowflake's newest attempt at an AI layer that learns the business from signals it already has. Treat it as preview, and note that it learns from data usage rather than from budget approvals or overrides.

technical: Corporate and enterprise performance management are software categories covering budgeting, planning, forecasting, consolidation, close, reporting and analytics with finance-owned models, workflow and controls.
sales: The category of software Vena, Anaplan, OneStream and others sell for running planning and close. The real build versus buy question is whether to configure one of these products or build one from data platform parts.

technical: Vena's in-memory multidimensional engine of dimensions, hierarchies and members, paired with relational storage for high transaction volumes, which serves as the governed model Vena AI operates on.
sales: The finance cube at the heart of Vena where plans, actuals and versions live. It plays the role a semantic layer plays on data platforms, and it also supports input, versions and workflow.

technical: Converting entity results from their functional currency into the reporting currency using rules such as average rates for income statement items, closing rates for balance sheet items and historical rates for equity, with differences booked to a translation reserve.
sales: Turning results in euros or pesos into the group's reporting currency at the right rates. Getting the rate rules right is accounting logic that a homegrown build must design, test and maintain.

technical: A Databricks service for hosting custom web applications built with frameworks such as Dash, Flask and Streamlit, with a managed service principal and native Lakebase connection, billed in DBUs per hour by compute size.
sales: A place to run custom-built apps on Databricks. Databricks documents its write-back pattern with a simple to-do app template, which shows that a planning interface would be custom development.

technical: The Databricks Unit, a normalized unit of compute consumption billed at rates that vary by product, tier and cloud. Genie, Databricks Apps and model serving are billed in DBUs.
sales: The meter Databricks bills on. Genie is free for people using it through January 31, 2027, so pilot costs understate long-run cost.

technical: A Power BI storage mode that reads Delta tables directly from OneLake into memory without import, announced GA on OneLake at FabCon 2026.
sales: A way for Power BI reports to read Fabric data live without copying it in. Note that Fabric Planning needs a gateway with fixed credentials, not single sign-on, when connected to these models.

technical: A modeling approach in which plan values are calculated from operational drivers, such as headcount times salary rate or units times price, with dependent values recalculated when a driver changes.
sales: Planning from the business levers people understand, like volume and price, instead of typing every line. It needs a calculation engine that recalculates on save, which data platforms do not provide out of the box.

technical: The unit of shared compute in Microsoft Fabric, sold as F SKUs from F2 to F8192, with one or three year reservations saving about 41% over pay-as-you-go, and consumed by workloads including Copilot, data agents and Planning.
sales: The prepaid pool of computing power a company buys for Fabric. Because Planning and AI draw from the same pool, Microsoft can position them as already paid for, so ask about real consumption at full use.

technical: Conversational agents in Fabric, GA since FabCon in March 2026, that generate read-only SQL, DAX and KQL over up to five sources such as lakehouses, warehouses and semantic models, with answers capped at 25 rows by 25 columns and English-only support.
sales: Microsoft's ask-your-data assistants on Fabric. They cannot change data and only work in English, which matters for bilingual Canadian finance teams.

technical: Microsoft's enterprise intelligence layer in Fabric that grounds data in business language for people and agents, with Power BI semantic models (GA) and Ontology (preview) as core items and Graph (preview), data agents, operations agents and Planning (GA) as supporting items.
sales: Microsoft's umbrella for business context, AI and planning on Fabric. It is the closest platform match to a context layer with planning, and it bills on capacity many prospects already own.

technical: Combining the financial results of multiple legal entities into group statements, including currency translation, intercompany eliminations, ownership and minority interest calculations, and top-side adjustments.
sales: Rolling up all the subsidiaries into one set of group numbers that auditors accept. No data platform reviewed offers it natively, while Vena's advanced consolidation went GA on August 26, 2026.

technical: A delivery model in which vendor engineers embed with a customer to build and adapt solutions on the vendor's platform. Snowflake points finance customers to Forward Deployed Finance Specialists, and Palantir is known for this approach.
sales: Vendor engineers who come in to build a custom solution. It signals that the platform has no packaged planning product, so the customer ends up owning a custom application.

technical: Google's enterprise agent workspace, formerly Agentspace, where users reach Google and partner agents, build no-code agents with Agent Designer and use agents built with ADK. Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services, in preview since August 25, 2026, targets banking use cases rather than FP&A.
sales: Google's front door for company-wide AI assistants. Its finance edition targets banks and investment research, not corporate budgeting.

technical: Databricks' natural-language analytics family. Genie Agents (renamed from Genie spaces in July 2026) answer questions over curated tables with read-only queries under each user's permissions, and Genie One (renamed from Databricks One) is the business-user agent app, both GA, with usage by people free through January 31, 2027.
sales: Databricks' ask-your-data assistant for business users. Its generated queries are always read-only, so it can explain the numbers but cannot update a plan.

technical: A Databricks context layer in public preview that combines Unity Catalog semantics with snippets inferred from dashboards, SQL queries and Genie Agents, each ranked by an authority score based on source, usage and freshness.
sales: The Databricks feature closest to context that grows with use. It learns from analytics activity like dashboards and queries rather than from planning events like approvals and overrides.

technical: Snowflake tables, part of Unistore, that add a row store with row-level locking and enforced primary, foreign and unique keys for transactional workloads next to analytics. Snowflake declared them GA in November 2024, though one third party still calls them preview.
sales: Snowflake's way of handling many small, fast updates, which planning input requires. A secondary source reports they lack time travel, which would push plan history into custom tables.

technical: Consolidation entries that remove balances and transactions between entities in the same group, such as intercompany sales, receivables and payables, so group results reflect only external activity, usually after intercompany matching.
sales: Removing sales and balances between a company's own subsidiaries so revenue is not counted twice. It is a core reason finance teams buy a CPM product rather than build one.

technical: SAP's AI assistant and agent front end that orchestrates workflows, data and more than 200 specialized agents through over 50 domain assistants. The Financial Planning Assistant and Joule Agents in SAP Enterprise Planning were scheduled for GA in Q3 2026, delivery was not verified, and Joule Studio MCP and A2A support is described as future.
sales: SAP's AI copilot across its applications. Its planning agents were due in Q3 2026, while Vena's Planning Agent has been GA since May 2026.

technical: Google Cloud's metadata and governance catalog, renamed from Dataplex Universal Catalog on April 10, 2026, which brings BigQuery measures and LookML together. Automated context curation of descriptions, glossaries and verified SQL is in preview.
sales: Google's catalog of what data means and who owns it, previously called Dataplex. One analyst firm calls it more of a metadata aggregator than a true business context layer.

technical: The author-curated set of semantic definitions attached to a Genie Agent, including table descriptions, joins, SQL expressions, example SQL and instructions. Feedback generates suggestions, but Databricks states agent behavior does not change from user feedback alone.
sales: The hand-maintained notes that teach a Genie assistant how the data works. Someone on the data team has to keep them current.

technical: Databricks' managed serverless PostgreSQL service for transactional workloads, with autoscaling, zero-copy branching, point-in-time recovery and sync to Delta tables. GA on AWS in February 2026, with Azure in beta at that time.
sales: A transactional database inside Databricks that custom apps can save data to. Its branching copies a database, which is not the same as managing budget and forecast versions.

technical: Databricks' data engineering suite, including Lakeflow Connect managed connectors (for example NetSuite, Workday and Dynamics 365), Lakeflow Designer for no-code pipelines and Lakeflow Jobs for orchestration.
sales: Databricks' tools for bringing in and moving data. Lakeflow Jobs schedules data pipelines and is not a budget approval workflow.

technical: Google's BI platform built on the LookML semantic model, with Conversational Analytics in Looker (GA) and newer agentic features such as dashboard agents and a managed Looker MCP server in preview.
sales: Google's reporting tool, known for consistent metric definitions. Its only documented write-back to BigQuery is a reference pattern that only appends rows, which is far from planning input.

technical: Looker's code-based modeling language that defines dimensions, measures, joins and Explores over SQL databases, maintained by developers with Git version control and continuous integration.
sales: The language Looker uses to define business metrics, maintained by developers in code. It is a strong reporting semantic layer, but it has no concept of plan input, versions or scenarios.

technical: Google's open-source MCP server framework, version 1.0 GA, that exposes database and analytics tools, including BigQuery conversational analytics and TimesFM forecasting, to MCP clients and ADK agents as a self-managed alternative to Google's managed MCP servers.
sales: A free Google toolkit that lets AI assistants query company databases. It speeds up building agents but does not add planning features.

technical: Unity Catalog objects, defined in YAML, SQL or a low-code editor, that separate measures from dimensions so metrics are defined once and queried by any grouping, with star and snowflake joins, window measures and materialization. GA per Databricks, though one third-party recap lists them as preview.
sales: Databricks' semantic layer for KPIs, feeding dashboards, Genie and outside BI tools. Data engineers usually maintain them, not finance.

technical: Microsoft's family of AI assistants, including Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot in Fabric and Power BI, which consumes Fabric capacity units. Copilot in Fabric processes data in the US and EU data boundaries, so Canadian data is processed cross-geo.
sales: Microsoft's AI assistant across Office, Teams and Power BI. Vena works inside it, since the Vena MCP server supports Microsoft Copilot as a client and Vena Copilot runs in Teams.

technical: Microsoft's data governance, security and compliance suite, providing data loss prevention, access restriction policies, audit and eDiscovery that apply to Fabric data agents and Copilot interactions.
sales: Microsoft's compliance toolset that protects and logs AI conversations about company data. It is a genuine governance strength for Microsoft and a standard expectation for any AI tool in finance.

technical: An open-source platform, deeply integrated in Databricks, for tracking, evaluating and monitoring machine learning and generative AI applications. MLflow 3 attaches scorers such as LLM judges and code checks to traces before release and on production traffic.
sales: The quality-control system Databricks teams use to test AI before and after launch. Using it well is part of the ongoing engineering cost of building your own agents.

technical: Morpheo AI Inc., a Toronto agentic data platform company acquired by Vena (announced July 28, closed August 18, 2026). Its Morpheo Omega data-product technology and connectors became the foundation of Vena Omega, GA November 17, 2026.
sales: The AI data company Vena bought to build Omega. It brings the connectors that pull in data from anywhere in the business and the technology that turns it into context.

technical: Databricks' brand for its generative AI tooling, whose Mosaic AI Agent Framework is now marketed under the Agent Bricks umbrella as Custom Agents on Apps.
sales: An older Databricks name reps will still see in decks and documents. Treat it as part of Agent Bricks.

technical: The single, tenant-wide data lake under Microsoft Fabric, storing data in open Delta format and exposing outside data in place through shortcuts or as managed replicas through mirroring.
sales: Microsoft Fabric's one data lake for the whole company. Fabric Planning reads from it, and Vena's six Microsoft Fabric data integrations connect to the same Microsoft data estate.

technical: Palantir action types define a single transaction that changes one or more Ontology objects using user-defined logic, with rules, submission criteria, per-action permissions, side effects to external systems and action logs with full audit history.
sales: Palantir's governed way to change data, with permissions and a full audit log. It is a generic building block, so budget submission and approval would need to be designed on top.

technical: A vendor-neutral, Apache 2.0 specification for exchanging semantic definitions (data sets, metrics, dimensions, relationships and contexts) across tools. Snowflake published the first version January 27, 2026, recaps describe it as finalized at Summit 2026 with 54 vendors, and a secondary source reports it entered the Apache Incubator as Apache Ossie.
sales: An industry standard so metric definitions can move between tools instead of being rebuilt in each one. Databricks, dbt Labs and Salesforce are members, but no planning vendor appears on the published member list.

technical: Snowflake's managed data ingestion service based on Apache NiFi for batch and streaming pipelines, GA since May 2025, with second-generation deployments and runtimes GA September 8, 2026 and gen-2 connectors such as PostgreSQL and MySQL CDC still in public preview.
sales: Snowflake's tool for bringing data in from other systems. It moves actuals into Snowflake, which is the first step of any build on Snowflake.

technical: Databricks' open protocol for live, cross-platform table sharing without copying, renamed from Delta Sharing in June 2026 and hosted by the Linux Foundation.
sales: The way Databricks lets other tools read its tables directly. Planning vendors such as Pigment use it only to import data, with no write-back.

technical: A Vena feature in open beta from the Spring 2026 release for creating, managing and using relational data directly within Excel, with the option to push that data into Power BI Desktop.
sales: A way to keep operational detail, such as headcount records or project lists, alongside financial plans in Vena. It is in open beta, so confirm availability before promising it.

technical: Palantir's AI platform on Foundry, including AIP Logic, Chatbot Studio (formerly AIP Agent Studio), Threads, Assist, Evals and pro-code agents built with the Claude, OpenAI or Google agent SDKs and bound to the Ontology.
sales: Palantir's AI layer for building assistants and AI workflows on the Ontology. It is powerful, and any finance agents would be custom-built.

technical: Palantir's data integration and application platform centered on the Ontology, with pipelines, Workshop applications and AIP for AI workflows, sold under enterprise contracts with AIP usage priced in compute-seconds.
sales: Palantir's platform for building bespoke operational and decision apps on company data. It can power a custom planning app, but the planning model, calculations, approvals and Excel experience would all be built.

technical: Foundry's semantic and operational layer of object types, properties, links, actions and functions that serves as both the business model and the governed write-back layer, exposed to outside agents through Ontology MCP with controlled writes.
sales: Palantir's model of the business, which also controls how data gets changed. Architecturally it is the closest match to context plus actions, but every finance concept must be modeled by the customer.

technical: Controls that freeze data for closed periods, submitted entities or approved versions so values cannot change without an authorized unlock, sometimes delegated to data owners. SAP Analytics Cloud calls this data locking.
sales: Freezing last month or an approved budget so nobody changes it after the fact. It protects the numbers that went to the board.

technical: Microsoft's first-party EPM and CPM workload in Fabric IQ, built by Lumel, for budgets, forecasts, scenarios and variance analysis, writing back to Fabric SQL databases. GA by mid-2026 with billing on Fabric capacity from August 1, 2026, and documented limits include one semantic model per plan item and 1.2 million cells per write-back.
sales: Microsoft's own budgeting and forecasting tool inside Fabric, and the most direct competitor in Microsoft-centric accounts. Probe consolidation, native Excel use and what its AI does today, since Microsoft lists agentic planning as roadmap.

technical: The governed tabular model in Power BI and Fabric, formerly called a dataset, holding tables, relationships, DAX measures, hierarchies and row-level security, now enriched with AI instructions and verified answers for Copilot (preview).
sales: The model most Power BI finance reports already run on. Microsoft now reuses it as AI context and as the base for Fabric Planning, which is a strong advantage in Power BI shops.

technical: A forecast updated on a regular cadence that always extends a fixed number of periods ahead, such as 12 or 18 months, adding a new period as each one closes instead of stopping at fiscal year end.
sales: A forecast that always looks a year or more ahead instead of ending in December. It means refreshing data and revisiting assumptions more often, which raises the value of automation and of remembering past assumptions.

technical: AWS's unified data and AI workspace, GA March 13, 2025, that brings together EMR, Glue, Athena and Redshift tools with lakehouse data access and governance through SageMaker Catalog, which can enforce business glossary terms.
sales: Amazon's one-stop workspace for data and AI teams. It governs and prepares data well, but it is a toolset for engineers, not an application for planners.

technical: The planning capabilities of SAP Analytics Cloud, including cell-level data entry with rolldown, private and published versions, data locking, data actions, structured allocations, validation rules, value driver trees and an Excel add-in with write-back.
sales: SAP's real planning tool and the most direct full-stack competitor in SAP ERP accounts. Ask what is shipped versus scheduled for its AI agents, and how it handles entities that run on other ERPs.

technical: SAP's business data fabric combining Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, HANA Cloud, BW and SAP Databricks with curated SAP data products, sold in Capacity Units and required to be bought with at least one Intelligent Application. BDC Connect shares data zero-copy with Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery and Fabric.
sales: SAP's data platform for SAP and partner data, bundled with its analytics and planning tools. It is strongest where the business runs on SAP and it carries commercial lock-in signals.

technical: SAP's data warehousing and modeling service inside Business Data Cloud that federates SAP and non-SAP data. With seamless planning, SAP Analytics Cloud planning models store their data in Datasphere spaces.
sales: SAP's data warehouse layer under its planning and analytics tools. Seamless planning requires SAC on HANA Cloud, one-to-one SAC and Datasphere tenants and the same data center.

technical: A structured map of business entities, processes and relationships that SAP announced at Sapphire in May 2026 as the foundation of the SAP Business AI Platform, building on the knowledge graph component SAP added to Datasphere in 2025.
sales: SAP's map of how its business objects connect, used to give Joule agents context. It is strongest on SAP master data and processes.

technical: Alternative sets of assumptions and their calculated outcomes, such as base, upside and downside, stored and compared alongside versions. A persisted scenario differs from a one-off what-if question answered by an AI agent.
sales: Modeling what happens if growth slows or a price increase lands, and keeping those cases to compare. Many data platform agents can answer a what-if question, but they do not save the scenario into a governed plan.
related: Vena Planning, Query and Reporting agents

technical: A Snowflake feature, GA February 3, 2026, that generates and updates semantic views from query history, BI dashboards such as Tableau and Power BI, and trusted SQL, proposing changes that data teams review and certify. One third-party recap lists it as preview, possibly reflecting newer sub-features.
sales: Snowflake software that learns business definitions by watching how people already query data. It is a real, shipping example of context that improves with use, though it learns from analytics rather than from planning cycles.

technical: Schema-level Snowflake database objects that define tables, relationships, facts, dimensions and metrics for BI tools and Cortex Analyst, replacing YAML semantic models. GA for querying since August 26, 2025.
sales: Snowflake's semantic layer, where business definitions of metrics live. They describe reporting data and do not include plan versions, input or approval logic.

technical: Snowflake's packaged agent application for business users, with charts, artifacts, automations, skills, Deep Research and per-user memory, inheriting row-access and column-level policies. Renamed from Snowflake Intelligence at Summit 2026 in June, and the preview status of features such as User Memory is reported inconsistently.
sales: Snowflake's ready-made AI assistant for business users, previously called Snowflake Intelligence. Its memory is personal to each user, not shared memory of the finance team's planning decisions.

technical: Snowflake's built-in governance and discovery capabilities, covering access policies, classification, lineage and AI guardrails. Horizon Context, announced at Summit 2026 and reported in private preview, collects and enriches metadata from outside sources through five connectors.
sales: The governance layer inside Snowflake that controls who sees what and documents data. It helps prove data is trusted, but it is not a planning or approval workflow.

technical: Applications packaged with the Snowflake Native App Framework that install and run inside a customer's Snowflake account. Support for Cortex Agents and Snowflake-managed MCP servers inside Native Apps went GA August 7, 2026.
sales: A way for software vendors to ship an app that runs inside the customer's own Snowflake account. It is the route any third party, including a CPM vendor, could use to deliver an AI planning agent in Snowflake.

technical: Managed PostgreSQL instances that run inside Snowflake, GA February 24, 2026 in selected AWS and Azure regions, suited to transactional application state and write-back.
sales: A standard transactional database now available inside Snowflake. It gives builders a place to save plan inputs, but versions, workflow and calculations still have to be built around it.

technical: Snowflake's internal long-range planning application for 40+ entities, built by its finance team on Snowflake, Streamlit and the CoCo coding agent, with write-back, versioned scenarios, role-based review and row-level controls. Described in a July 8, 2026 blog that discloses no team size or cost.
sales: Proof that a data platform company had to build its own planning app, with its own engineers, on its own platform. It shows planning on Snowflake is possible, and also that it is a custom software project.

technical: Spreading pushes a value entered at a summary level down to lower-level members or periods by a method such as even, seasonal or prior-year pattern, while breakback adjusts the detail proportionally when a parent total is changed.
sales: Entering an annual number and having it fall into months, or changing a total and having the detail adjust automatically. Finance users expect this in any planning grid, and it is a significant build item on a data platform.

technical: Snowflake's hosted Streamlit environment for building Python data apps with interactive inputs that run against Snowflake data. Cortex Agents APIs require its container runtime rather than the warehouse runtime.
sales: A quick way for developers to build simple web apps on Snowflake. Snowflake's own finance team used it as the input screen for its internal planning app, Snowplan.

technical: A GA Power BI capability that lets report users add, edit or delete data and call external APIs from a report, executed by Fabric user data functions against Fabric SQL databases, warehouses or lakehouse files.
sales: Buttons in a Power BI report that save changes back to the database. It is a general-purpose write-back building block, not a planning process with versions and approvals.

technical: Databricks' unified governance layer for data and AI assets, providing access control including ABAC, lineage, auditing, metric views and business semantics. At Data + AI Summit 2026 its Glossary was listed as preview coming soon and Domains as public preview.
sales: Databricks' central catalog and permission system. It governs who can read data and what it means, while plan input, approval and versioning sit outside its scope.

technical: Serverless Python functions in Fabric that read and write Fabric SQL databases, warehouses and lakehouse files and can be called from reports, pipelines, notebooks, Activator rules or REST.
sales: Small pieces of custom code that handle saving and logic behind Fabric apps. They are how a builder would let an AI agent write to Fabric, which is custom work.

technical: Comparing actuals with budget, forecast or prior periods across dimensions, quantifying the differences and attributing them to drivers such as price, volume or mix, usually with written commentary.
sales: Explaining why results differ from plan, the core monthly conversation in FP&A. AI can draft the analysis, but the commentary and decisions are exactly the history a cumulative context engine aims to keep.

technical: Vena's AI assistant built on Microsoft Azure OpenAI and the CubeFLEX model, introduced in beta April 3, 2024, which inherits Vena data, application and individual permissions and hosts Vena's named agents. Vena Copilot for Microsoft Teams has been GA since May 15, 2025.
sales: Vena's built-in AI assistant for finance users, available inside Vena and Microsoft Teams. It respects existing permissions, and Vena states customer data is never used to train public AI models.
related: Vena Planning, Query and Reporting agents

technical: Vena's MCP server, GA May 13, 2026, connects Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot to live Vena data under each user's existing data and application permissions. Developer docs list read tools only, while release materials announce plan updates and write-back.
sales: Lets a customer's preferred AI assistant work with live Vena data. Say read access is documented and write-back is announced until the developer docs change.

technical: Vena's cumulative context engine for finance, GA November 17, 2026. It combines governed data from across the business with definitions, assumptions, drivers, approvals and past decisions in user, industry, business and planning layers, and serves that context to Vena agents, Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI and MCP clients. Built on technology from the Morpheo acquisition.
sales: The brain under all of Vena's tools. It learns how your finance team plans and decides, keeps that knowledge, and makes every answer and forecast better the more you use it.

term: Vena Planning, Query and Reporting agents
technical: Named Vena Copilot agents, with the Planning Agent (GA May 13, 2026) generating forecasts, updating plans and applying scenario logic in natural language, the Query Agent (GA, Spring 2026) turning plain English into MQL, and the Reporting Agent (GA) working in the Ad Hoc tool. A Scenario Agent is listed as coming soon.
sales: Vena's shipped AI agents that answer questions and, in the Planning Agent's case, update plans inside governed workflows. That is a key contrast with data platform agents, which are read-only.

technical: Distinct, persistent copies of plan data such as Budget, Forecast 3+9 or Actuals, held in a version dimension with lifecycle states like open, locked and archived so they can be compared and promoted.
sales: Keeping Budget, each forecast and actuals side by side without overwriting each other. Database branching, such as Lakebase's, is not the same thing, because finance versions need business rules, locking and comparison.

technical: Process orchestration for planning cycles, including a budget calendar, task assignment, submission, review, rejection and approval routing, notifications and status tracking for each contributor.
sales: Making sure every department submits on time and the right people sign off. Snowflake's Multi-Party Approval and Databricks' Lakeflow Jobs sound similar but are admin and data controls, not budget workflows.

technical: Saving user- or system-entered values, such as budget inputs or forecast changes, back into the model's storage so they are immediately available to calculations, reports and other users.
sales: Typing a number into the plan and having it saved where everyone can use it. On data platforms this usually means custom development, for example Databricks' Excel add-in only overwrites whole tables, while Vena writes back natively from Excel.
